raw_case_text:
A 31-year-old male presented to the emergency room complaining of progressive dyspnea and productive cough over the course of 4 months. He also noted decreased appetite with a 50-pound weight loss over the past 5 months. He had no significant past medical or surgical history and was not taking any medications. His family history was unremarkable. He quit smoking tobacco two months ago due to worsening respiratory status; he rarely used alcohol and never used recreational drugs. He was unmarried and in a long-term heterosexual relationship and denied multiple sexual partners. He was currently working in an automobile parts factory as a janitor. After high school he had enlisted in the army and served for four years; at that time he was stationed in Hawaii. While in Hawaii he visited a single prostitute on several occasions.
Initial vital signs revealed temperature was 99.9 F, blood pressure 128/83 mmHg, pulse 134 beats per minute, and respiratory rate 22 breaths/minute; oxygen saturation was 92% on room air. He was in moderate respiratory distress, yet was awake, alert, and cooperative. Extraocular muscles were intact; there was no nystagmus or scleral icterus. Pupils were equal, round, and reactive to light. He had thrush under his tongue and on the palate. There was no palpable lymphadenopathy. Heart rate was regular with no murmurs, rubs, or gallops by auscultation. There were no palpable thrills. He had equal chest rise bilaterally. Breath sounds were diminished throughout, with rales and dullness to percussion in the lower lung fields bilaterally. Sensory and motor examination was grossly intact.
Laboratory data revealed white blood count 13,900/mcL, hemoglobin 7.2 g/dL, platelets 370,000/mcL, sodium 131 mmol/L potassium 5.8 mmol/L, chloride 99 mmol/L, carbon dioxide 17 mmol/L, blood urea nitrogen 155 mg/dL, and serum creatinine 8.9 mg/dL. Arterial blood gases showed a pH of 7.39, pCO2 32.2 mmHg, bicarbonate 19.1 mmol/L, and pO2 74.5 mmHg on 3 L nasal cannula. Chest X-ray showed diffuse bilateral reticulonodular opacities (Figure 1). He was found to be HIV positive with CD4 count of <5 cells/cc and viral load of 1,180,000 copies. Bronchoalveolar lavage was preformed; Grocott's methenamine silver stain of the washings demonstrated Pneumocystis jiroveci (Figure 2). He received antibiotics and steroids with gradual improvement.
On hospital day 14, he became confused and acutely developed nystagmus with both a horizontal and prominent vertical component. He was also found to have ataxia with finger to nose testing and difficulty sitting up without support. Considering his immunosuppressed state, infectious and neoplastic etiologies were the primary diagnostic considerations. Lumbar puncture revealed clear CSF, normal opening pressure, and normal cell counts. Polymerase chain reactions for Epstein-Barr virus, Herpes simplex virus, cytomegalovirus, and John Cunningham (JC) virus were negative. Nontreponemal serological screening for syphilis (VDRL), toxoplasmosis antibody, and Cryptococcus antigen titers were negative. CT of the head did not show any intracranial mass, hemorrhage, or other acute findings. MRI of the brain revealed a slight increase in T2 signal within the medial aspect of thalamus bilaterally (Figure 3). After excluding infection and neoplasm, the clinical diagnosis of Wernicke's encephalopathy was made. Intravenous thiamine was administered resulting in resolution of symptoms, which confirmed the diagnosis.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 31-year-old male factory janitor presented to the emergency department with a 4-month history of progressive dyspnea and productive cough, anorexia, and a 50-lb weight loss over 5 months.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Over the 4–5 months prior to presentation, the patient developed progressively worsening shortness of breath, productive cough (prompting him to quit smoking 2 months prior), poor appetite, and an unintentional 50-lb weight loss. On hospital day 14, while improving from pneumonia, he developed acute confusion, horizontal and vertical nystagmus, appendicular dysmetria, and severe truncal ataxia.
subjective.past_medical_history: No known prior medical or surgical history. Former tobacco smoker (quit 2 months prior), rare alcohol use, no illicit drug use. U.S. Army veteran stationed in Hawaii for 4 years after high school, where he had sexual contact with a female commercial sex worker on several occasions; currently in a monogamous heterosexual relationship.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for progressive dyspnea, productive cough, anorexia, and 50-lb weight loss over 5 months; subsequent inpatient confusion, nystagmus, and ataxia on day 14. No home medications.

objective.physical_examination: Initial vital signs: temperature 99.9 °F, blood pressure 128/83 mmHg, heart rate 134 beats/min, respiratory rate 22 breaths/min, and SpO2 92% on room air. Alert and in moderate respiratory distress with sublingual and palatal oral thrush, no palpable lymphadenopathy, diminished breath sounds throughout with bibasilar rales and dullness to percussion, and normal baseline neurological exam. On hospital day 14, neurological examination revealed acute confusion, prominent horizontal and vertical nystagmus, bilateral finger-to-nose dysmetria, and severe truncal ataxia (inability to sit unsupported).
objective.routine_investigations: Admission labs showed leukocytosis (WBC 13,900/µL), severe anemia (hemoglobin 7.2 g/dL), platelets 370,000/µL, hyponatremia (sodium 131 mmol/L), hyperkalemia (potassium 5.8 mmol/L), chloride 99 mmol/L, bicarbonate 17 mmol/L, severe azotemia (BUN 155 mg/dL, creatinine 8.9 mg/dL), and ABG on 3 L nasal cannula showing pH 7.39, pCO2 32.2 mmHg, HCO3- 19.1 mmol/L, and pO2 74.5 mmHg. Serum VDRL, Toxoplasma antibodies, and cryptococcal antigen were negative. Chest X-ray showed diffuse bilateral reticulonodular opacities.
objective.advanced_workup: Admission CD4+ T-cell count was <5 cells/mm3. Bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) Grocott methenamine silver (GMS) stain demonstrated Pneumocystis jirovecii cysts. Day 14 head CT was unremarkable; lumbar puncture showed clear CSF with normal opening pressure, normal cell counts, and negative CSF PCRs for EBV, HSV, CMV, and JC virus. Brain MRI demonstrated bilateral symmetric T2 hyperintensity in the medial thalami.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Newly diagnosed advanced HIV/AIDS (CD4+ count <5 cells/mm3, plasma HIV viral load 1,180,000 copies/mL) presenting with Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia (confirmed on BAL GMS stain), oral candidiasis, and severe acute renal failure (creatinine 8.9 mg/dL), complicated on hospital day 14 by non-alcoholic Wernicke encephalopathy secondary to severe malnutrition and 50-lb wasting (confirmed by classic triad of encephalopathy, horizontal/vertical nystagmus, and ataxia, bilateral medial thalamic T2 hyperintensity on brain MRI, negative CSF opportunistic infection workup, and rapid complete neurological resolution following intravenous thiamine administration).
